r.name: Bluebell Trail at Buckland Abbey
r.description: In late April / early May, the woodland is carpeted with a sea of bluebells and wild garlic. It's a wonderful time to enjoy this circular & take in the sights, sounds & smells of spring in the Devon countryside. Some uphill slopes, uneveness & steps.

r.name: Yellow Walk, Buckland Abbey
r.description: Start from the Cart pond, taking in views of the Tavy Valley. Step free, buggy & tramper friendly.

r.name: Saltram pillars walk, Saltram
r.description: This circular walk follows the Run England 1-mile route. The walk, which includes some slopes, can be muddy when wet.

r.name: Saltram boundary walk, Saltram
r.description: This walk includes a steep section with steps. The ground can get muddy, especially after wet weather, so walking boots are recommended.

r.name: Riverside cycle trail at Saltram
r.description: Perfect for families, young children, and those new to cycling, the terrain is largely flat with one steep hill.

r.name: Turnpike Trail, Saltram
r.description: This there & back walk starts in the car park and takes you to the start of the country park. One short incline (25m) along route (1 in 7), with the narrowest width of 2.2m. Seasonal dog access in accordance to livestock.

r.name: Wixenford Way, Saltram
r.description: This circular includes the adjoining turnpike trail & meadow path. Take in city views before reaching wildflower meadows. 1 short incline (25m, 1 in 7), with the majority of the route 3m wide & narrowest width of 2.2m. Seasonal dog access with livestock.

r.name: Cotehele to Bohetherick Woodland Walk, Cothele
r.description: This circular from Cotehele Quay takes you through Cotehele & Bohetherick Woods, exploring semi-natural ancient woodland and taking in the river and trees. Pass some of the finest old trees on the estate. Some hills, accessible parking & toilets available

r.name: Cotehele Circular Walk, Cothele
r.description: Explore Cotehele & discover hidden havens for wildlife. Take in the quay, stream & weir along to the Morden valley. Discover the secluded Cotehele Mill, then wander through the trees up to the house. Seasonally muddy paths & steep slope. Tramper available

r.name: Danescombe Valley Walk, Cothele
r.description: Starting at the Cotehele Quay car park, this trail through the picturesque Danescombe Valley passes fascinating relics from the area's rich mining history. Parts of the route are more challenging & not recommended for those with reduced mobility.
